subject: Private deployment — data access guardrails & operator scope
messages:
From: Andrew Simon <andrew.simon@lumahq.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, LumaHealth Procurement <procurement@lumahq.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on operator access + customer keys for private deploy

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are evaluating Redwood's private deployment for a PHI-bearing workload and want to lock down the operational boundary before moving forward. A few specific asks from security/procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood operators will ever be able to access unencrypted model inputs or outputs in a VPC/on-prem deployment when customer-managed keys (CMKs) are enabled?
- If operator access is needed for break-glass, what logging/audit trails are emitted and who holds the keys for those logs?
- Are there subprocessors involved in the Private control plane or instrumentation (e.g., telemetry, crash reporting)? If so, can you list them and their data scopes?
- Any cross-border data transfer considerations we should include in the DPA (our base is US-EAST; some patients in EU may be in scope later).

We have a draft DPA and a short compliance questionnaire attached. Happy to review with your team — procurement would like a short summary of guarantees (custody, operator scope, break-glass) before legal redlines.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are aiming to have an answer for the architecture review by next Friday.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Simon
Head of Security Engineering, LumaHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on operator access + customer keys for private deploy

Hi Andrew —

Thanks for outlining these so clearly. Short answers up front, details below and attached: redwood-dpa-draft-lumahq-v2.pdf (DPA markups) and operator-access-matrix.xlsx (proposed demarcation).

Summary:
- With customer-managed KMS keys configured in Private (VPC or on-prem), Redwood does not possess the plaintext keys and does not have runtime access to decrypt model inputs/outputs. All inference requests are encrypted in transit and at rest using the CMK.
- Break-glass: in extremely limited cases (hardware failure, emergency restore) an operator action may be required to assist with node-level recovery. Such actions do NOT decrypt application payloads; they operate at infrastructure/meta layer (node images, orchestration state). Any operator-initiated maintenance is gated by customer-approved, time-bound authorization and is logged with an immutable audit trail (timestamp, operator id, justification).
- Logs: system telemetry (node health, scheduler events) is emitted by the runtime; application-level logs containing user data are not captured when CMKs are in place. Audit logs referenced in the DPA are signed and stored in customer-controlled buckets when required.
- Subprocessors: for Private we rely on two third-parties for control-plane orchestration in hosted mode (not in air-gapped on-prem): a managed telemetry queue and a storage provider for software images. We list them in section 3.2 of the attached DPA draft with exact scopes and SOC2 references. For pure on-prem installs you may opt for a no-external-subprocessor deployment.
- Cross-border: data egress does not occur by default; any diagnostic bundles or telemetry are only exported with explicit customer consent and are subject to region filters; we call out EU transfer controls in the DPA addendum.

Attached are proposed contract language snippets for: operator scope, break-glass workflow, KMS responsibilities, and a subprocessors appendix. Key distinctions we propose: 1) Redwood will not hold keys nor have access to plaintext application data with CMK enabled; 2) operator actions are limited to orchestration-level interventions; 3) any operator access must be customer-initiated and time-limited with signed audit entries.

Next steps:
- Can procurement/legal at LumaHealth review the DPA markups (attached) and flag any redlines?
- We suggest a 45-minute technical handoff with your security and infra teams to walk the operator-access matrix and DPA snippets; propose Tue Jul 24 or Wed Jul 25.

Pinning Karthik (solutions) and Laura (legal enablement) to help with specifics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on operator access + customer keys for private deploy

Andrew —

Quick legal notes after reviewing Marissa's attachments: 

- DPA: We'll add a short subclause that requires Redwood to provide a signed export of audit logs within 48 hours on lawful request (we can make it contractual). Also adding explicit language that any telemetry redaction must be verified by you prior to export.
- Subprocessors: For hosted Private control plane we enumerate the two vendors and include the right to object within 10 business days after signature. For air-gapped installs, clause will state no external subprocessors will receive customer data.
- Escrow/KMS: If you require a KMS escrow solution, we can scope an addendum. Our standard is customer-managed keys; escrow is an optional enterprise feature (extra cost).

I'll prepare clean DPA language and mark the procurement-required summary page. Also, a note for engineering: we need to tighten the break-glass playbook so the audit artifacts include operator session recordings (where policy allows) and signed attestations. Karthik, can you confirm that the runtime can produce deterministic signed audit bundles?

Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Questions on operator access + customer keys for private deploy — next steps

Andrew — forwarding consolidated notes and next steps. See summary below and attached link to the private-deploy playbook.

Summary of commitments (Redwood):
1) Custody: Customer-managed KMS only (no plaintext key possession by Redwood).
2) Operator scope: Operators limited to orchestration and infra-level actions; no access to application-layer plaintext when CMK enabled.
3) Break-glass: Customer-initiated, time-limited authorization with signed audit bundle emitted to a customer-specified bucket.
4) Subprocessors: For hosted control-plane deployments we list two subprocessors in the DPA appendix; for on-prem/air-gapped installs no subprocessors will receive customer data.
5) Audit & evidence: We will provide signed audit logs and an export within 48 hours on request; diagnostic bundles require explicit consent and redaction verification by LumaHealth.

Action items:
- LumaHealth to review the attached DPA markups and return any legal redlines by EOD Tue Jul 25. (Andrew / procurement)
- Schedule a 45-min tech handoff (Marissa / Karthik) — propose Jul 24 at 10:30 AM PT. Please confirm or propose alternate times.
- Redwood to surface an optional KMS-escrow commercial addendum if escrow is desired (Laura to draft).

Attachments/links:

- Operator matrix: operator-access-matrix.xlsx
- Playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/share/privdep-playbook (read-only)
